1	# Backlog
2	
3	Ideas captured for later, with enough notes to pick up cold.
4	
5	## Rewind mode (time-rollback continue)
6	
7	**Idea:** A third game mode where, instead of losing a life outright, death lets you
8	*rewind* a second or two to just before the fatal hit and resume (with brief
9	invincibility). Distinct from Lives mode — here the ball trajectories are *rewound*
10	too, not just continued.
11	
12	**Why it's harder than Lives mode:** Lives mode only needs a flag + invincibility
13	timer; the world keeps running forward. Rewind needs the world to actually go
14	*backwards*, which means recording and restoring full simulation state.
15	
16	**Sketch:**
17	- Keep a ring buffer of world snapshots, ~1 per frame for the last ~2–3s
18	  (e.g. 180 frames). Each snapshot stores: player x; every ball's
19	  `{textureKey, x, y, vx, vy, angularVelocity, scale}`; every pickup's
20	  `{value, x, y, vx, vy}`; `elapsed`/`collected`/`segment`.
21	- On death: pick the snapshot from ~1.2s before now, then rebuild the scene from it
22	  — destroy current balls/pickups, recreate from the snapshot (Arcade physics isn't
23	  deterministic to *replay*, but restoring a position+velocity snapshot is exact),
24	  rewind `elapsed`/score, grant invincibility, resume.
25	- Optional polish: a visual "rewind" effect (fast-reverse a few frames by stepping
26	  the buffer backwards before resuming, desaturate/scanline shader, a whoosh SFX).
27	- Limit uses (e.g. N rewinds per run) so it's not infinite, like Lives.
28	
29	**Cost / risk:** Memory for the buffer is small (a few hundred plain objects).
30	Main work is a clean serialize/restore of Ball/NumberPickup (their constructors take
31	indices, not raw state — would need a `fromSnapshot()` path or a restore method that
32	bypasses `launch()`/`configure()`). Moderate effort; well-contained.
33	
34	**Full plan:** see [docs/rewind-mode-plan.md](docs/rewind-mode-plan.md).
35	
36	**Status:** Not started. Lives mode (shipped, now with a heart economy) covers the
37	"more forgiving" need for now.
38
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Attack on Ball
2	
3	A doodle-style recreation of the classic **Attack on Ball** arcade game (originally
4	by *eggbones*, last updated 2017 and effectively gone from modern stores). Built
5	with **Phaser 4**, rendered in a hand-drawn "crayon" look with **rough.js**, and
6	shipped as an installable **PWA**.
7	
8	**▶ Play: https://daviddwlee84.github.io/AttackOnBall/**
9	
10	![hero](public/icons/icon-192.png)
11	
12	## Gameplay
13	
14	Move the green hero left/right along the water line. Balls of various sizes fly in
15	from both sides and bounce around the arena — get hit and it's game over. Survive
16	as long as you can: the timer (your score) counts up continuously, and walking over
17	the falling numbers adds those seconds straight to it. Every 10 seconds the arena
18	recolors. Difficulty ramps up: balls spawn faster and more pile on the longer you
19	last. Every ball is guaranteed to bounce above the hero's head, so it's always
20	dodgeable.
21	
22	**Controls**
23	
24	- Desktop: `←` / `→` or `A` / `D`
25	- Touch: tap or hold anywhere — the hero walks toward your finger
26	
27	**Settings (start screen)** — pick a difficulty preset (Easy / Medium / Hard / Crazy)
28	or open **Advanced settings** to tune move speed, gravity, ball speed/angle, spawn
29	rates and the difficulty ramp. Settings persist in the browser.
30	
31	## Develop
32	
33	```bash
34	npm install
35	npm run dev       # local dev server with hot reload
36	npm run build     # production build to dist/
37	npm run preview   # serve the production build locally
38	npm run smoke      # headless boot/play check against the preview server
39	```
40	
41	> `npm run smoke` requires the preview server running (`npm run preview`) and
42	> installs Puppeteer on demand; it is optional and CI-style only.
43	
44	## Architecture
45	
46	- `src/config.js` — fixed constants (render `SCALE`, arena size, palettes, ball
47	  sizes, pickup values). The whole game is authored at 960×540 and multiplied by
48	  `SCALE` for a crisp hi-DPI buffer.
49	- `src/settings.js` — runtime-configurable, persisted settings: difficulty presets
50	  + advanced physics/difficulty params. `gameParams()` returns SCALE-applied values
51	  the gameplay reads (via `scene.params`).
52	- `src/ui/settingsPanel.js` — the HTML settings overlay on the menu screen.
53	- `src/doodle.js` — rough.js texture generators (hero expressions, balls, numbers,
54	  fragments, grid). All art is generated procedurally at boot — no image assets.
55	- `src/scenes/` — `BootScene` (generates textures) → `MenuScene` (backdrop +
56	  settings panel) → `GameScene` (core loop) → `GameOverScene`.
57	- `src/objects/` — `Player`, `Ball`, `NumberPickup`.
58	- `src/systems/` — `spawner` (difficulty/density) and `arena` (background, timer
59	  bar, palette shuffle).
60	
61	The original vanilla-Canvas prototype lives in `deprecated/attack_on_ball_canvas.html`
62	for reference; the tuned physics constants were ported from it.
63	
64	## Deploy to GitHub Pages
65	
66	Already live (see link above). `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds with the
67	`/AttackOnBall/` base path (`GITHUB_PAGES=true`) and deploys `dist/` via GitHub
68	Actions on every push to `main`. Pages is configured with **Source: GitHub Actions**.
69	If you fork/rename, update `base` in `vite.config.js` to match the new repo name.
70
```
</details></tool-use>

    66	
    67	// A bouncing ball. Flies in from one side with a random speed + angle, arcs
    68	// under gravity, and bounces elastically on the ground (stable height). The
    69	// launch is clamped so its apex always clears the hero's head — keeping the
    70	// game winnable regardless of the random roll. Despawns once it sails off the
    71	// far side.
    72	//
    73	// Each ball owns a ground shadow that tracks its height (selling the bounce)
    74	// and squashes on landing; the scene drives this via tick() each frame.
    75	export default class Ball extends Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Sprite {
    76	  constructor(scene, sizeIdx, colorIdx) {
    77	    const size = BALL_SIZES[sizeIdx];
    78	    const fromLeft = Math.random() < 0.5;
    79	    const x = fromLeft ? -size.r : GAME_W + size.r;
    80	    // Spawn just above the floor so the launch velocity alone sets the (stable,
    81	    // elastic) bounce height — keeps balls in a predictable, threatening band.
    82	    const y = GROUND_Y - size.r - Math.random() * size.r;
    83	    super(scene, x, y, `ball-${sizeIdx}-${colorIdx}`);
    84	
    85	    scene.add.existing(this);
    86	    scene.physics.add.existing(this);
    87	
    88	    this.radius = size.r;
    89	    this.sizeIdx = sizeIdx;
    90	    this.dir = fromLeft ? 1 : -1;
    91	    this.wasOnFloor = false;
    92	
    93	    // Ground shadow, sized/faded each frame from the ball's height.
    94	    this.shadow = scene.add
    95	      .ellipse(x, GROUND_Y + 2, this.radius * 2, this.radius * 0.55, 0x000000, 0.22)
    96	      .setDepth(-1);
    97	  }
    98	
    99	  // Configure the body and apply the launch velocity. MUST be called *after* the
   100	  // ball is added to its physics group: adding to the group re-enables the body
   101	  // and resets gravity/bounce/velocity to the group defaults, so doing this in
   102	  // the constructor left balls flying in straight lines (no gravity, no bounce).
   103	  // `elapsed` (seconds survived) gently ramps launch speed for rising pressure.
   104	  launch(elapsed = 0) {
   105	    const p = this.scene.params;
   106	    const ramp = 1 + Math.min(p.speedRampCap, elapsed * p.speedRamp);
   107	    const speedLo = Math.min(p.ballSpeedMin, p.ballSpeedMax);
   108	    const speedHi = Math.max(p.ballSpeedMin, p.ballSpeedMax);
   109	    const speed = Phaser.Math.FloatBetween(speedLo, speedHi) * ramp;
   110	    const angLo = Math.min(p.angleMin, p.angleMax);
   111	    const angHi = Math.max(p.angleMin, p.angleMax);
   112	    const angle = Phaser.Math.DegToRad(Phaser.Math.FloatBetween(angLo, angHi));
   113	    let vx = Math.cos(angle) * speed * this.dir;
   114	    let vy = -Math.sin(angle) * speed;
   115	
   116	    // Playability guarantee: the bounce apex (vy^2 / 2g above the floor) must
   117	    // clear the hero's head plus a margin, or the ball would be undodgeable.
   118	    const minApex = PLAYER_SIZE + this.radius + p.minApexClearance;
   119	    const minVy = Math.sqrt(2 * p.gravity * minApex);
   120	    if (-vy < minVy) vy = -minVy;
   121	
   122	    this.body.setCircle(this.radius, PAD, PAD);
   123	    this.body.setAllowGravity(true);
   124	    this.body.setGravityY(p.gravity);
   125	    this.setBounce(0, p.ballBounce);
   126	    this.setVelocity(vx, vy);
   127	    this.setAngularVelocity(this.dir * Phaser.Math.Between(60, 200));
   128	    return this;
   129	  }

   132	  // ball's height and detect the landing edge to squash + kick up dust.
   133	  tick() {
   134	    const bottom = this.y + this.radius;
   135	    const height = Math.max(0, GROUND_Y - bottom); // px above the floor

   138	    this.shadow.setScale(t, t);
   139	    this.shadow.setAlpha(0.22 * t);

   153	  }

1	import * as Phaser from 'phaser';
2	import { GAME_W, GROUND_Y, BALL_SIZES, PLAYER_SIZE } from '../config.js';
3	import { PAD } from '../doodle.js';
4	import { Sfx } from '../audio.js';
5	
6	// A bouncing ball. Flies in from one side with a random speed + angle, arcs
7	// under gravity, and bounces elastically on the ground (stable height). The
8	// launch is clamped so its apex always clears the hero's head — keeping the
9	// game winnable regardless of the random roll. Despawns once it sails off the
10	// far side.
11	//
12	// Each ball owns a ground shadow that tracks its height (selling the bounce)
13	// and squashes on landing; the scene drives this via tick() each frame.
14	export default class Ball extends Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Sprite {
15	  constructor(scene, sizeIdx, colorIdx) {
16	    const size = BALL_SIZES[sizeIdx];
17	    const fromLeft = Math.random() < 0.5;
18	    const x = fromLeft ? -size.r : GAME_W + size.r;
19	    // Spawn just above the floor so the launch velocity alone sets the (stable,
20	    // elastic) bounce height — keeps balls in a predictable, threatening band.
21	    const y = GROUND_Y - size.r - Math.random() * size.r;
22	    super(scene, x, y, `ball-${sizeIdx}-${colorIdx}`);
23	
24	    scene.add.existing(this);
25	    scene.physics.add.existing(this);
26	
27	    this.radius = size.r;
28	    this.sizeIdx = sizeIdx;
29	    this.dir = fromLeft ? 1 : -1;
30	    this.wasOnFloor = false;
31	
32	    // Ground shadow, sized/faded each frame from the ball's height.
33	    this.shadow = scene.add
34	      .ellipse(x, GROUND_Y + 2, this.radius * 2, this.radius * 0.55, 0x000000, 0.22)
35	      .setDepth(-1);
36	  }
37	
38	  // Configure the body and apply the launch velocity. MUST be called *after* the
39	  // ball is added to its physics group: adding to the group re-enables the body
40	  // and resets gravity/bounce/velocity to the group defaults, so doing this in
41	  // the constructor left balls flying in straight lines (no gravity, no bounce).
42	  // `elapsed` (seconds survived) gently ramps launch speed for rising pressure.
43	  launch(elapsed = 0) {
44	    const p = this.scene.params;
45	    const ramp = 1 + Math.min(p.speedRampCap, elapsed * p.speedRamp);
46	    const speedLo = Math.min(p.ballSpeedMin, p.ballSpeedMax);
47	    const speedHi = Math.max(p.ballSpeedMin, p.ballSpeedMax);
48	    const speed = Phaser.Math.FloatBetween(speedLo, speedHi) * ramp;
49	    const angLo = Math.min(p.angleMin, p.angleMax);
50	    const angHi = Math.max(p.angleMin, p.angleMax);
51	    const angle = Phaser.Math.DegToRad(Phaser.Math.FloatBetween(angLo, angHi));
52	    let vx = Math.cos(angle) * speed * this.dir;
53	    let vy = -Math.sin(angle) * speed;
54	
55	    // Playability guarantee: the bounce apex (vy^2 / 2g above the floor) must
56	    // clear the hero's head plus a margin, or the ball would be undodgeable.
57	    const minApex = PLAYER_SIZE + this.radius + p.minApexClearance;
58	    const minVy = Math.sqrt(2 * p.gravity * minApex);
59	    if (-vy < minVy) vy = -minVy;
60	
61	    this.body.setCircle(this.radius, PAD, PAD);
62	    this.body.setAllowGravity(true);
63	    this.body.setGravityY(p.gravity);
64	    this.setBounce(0, p.ballBounce);
65	    this.setVelocity(vx, vy);
66	    this.setAngularVelocity(this.dir * Phaser.Math.Between(60, 200));
67	    return this;
68	  }
69	
70	  // Per-frame upkeep (called from GameScene.update): sync the shadow to the
71	  // ball's height and detect the landing edge to squash + kick up dust.
72	  tick() {
73	    const bottom = this.y + this.radius;
74	    const height = Math.max(0, GROUND_Y - bottom); // px above the floor
75	    const t = Phaser.Math.Clamp(1 - height / (260 * (this.radius / 36)), 0.25, 1);
76	    this.shadow.x = this.x;
77	    this.shadow.setScale(t, t);
78	    this.shadow.setAlpha(0.22 * t);
79	
80	    const onFloor = this.body.onFloor();
81	    if (onFloor && !this.wasOnFloor) this.land();
82	    this.wasOnFloor = onFloor;
83	  }
84	
85	  // Squash on impact, then spring back; ask the scene to puff dust.
86	  land() {
87	    this.scene.tweens.killTweensOf(this);
88	    this.setScale(1.28, 0.72);
89	    this.scene.tweens.add({ targets: this, scaleX: 1, scaleY: 1, duration: 200, ease: 'Back.out' });
90	    if (this.scene.spawnDust) this.scene.spawnDust(this.x, this.radius);
91	    Sfx.bounce(this.sizeIdx);
92	  }
93	
94	  // True once the ball has drifted well off either side and can be culled.
95	  isOffscreen() {
96	    return this.x < -2 * this.radius - 40 || this.x > GAME_W + 2 * this.radius + 40;
97	  }
98	
99	  destroy(fromScene) {
100	    if (this.shadow) {
101	      this.shadow.destroy();
102	      this.shadow = null;
103	    }
104	    super.destroy(fromScene);
105	  }
106	}
107

    23	export default class GameScene extends Phaser.Scene {

    28	  create() {

    30	    // entity is created — Player/Ball/Spawner all read scene.params.

    40	    // costs a life and grants brief invincibility while the balls keep flying.
    41	    this.mode = this.params.mode === 'lives' ? 'lives' : 'classic';
    42	    this.lives = this.mode === 'lives' ? Phaser.Math.Clamp(this.params.lives | 0, 1, 5) : 1;
    43	    this.maxLives = Math.max(MAX_LIVES, this.lives);

    50	    this.ground = this.add.rectangle(GAME_W / 2, GROUND_Y + GROUND_H / 2, GAME_W, GROUND_H);
    51	    this.ground.setVisible(false);

180	      this.scaleY = 1;

182	      this.angle = Math.sin(p * Math.PI * 6) * 16;
183	      const s = 1 + Math.sin(p * Math.PI * 6) * 0.05;
184	      this.scaleX = s;
185	      this.scaleY = 2 - s;
186	    } else {
187	      // hop: a couple of excited squash-and-stretch bounces in place
188	      this.angle = 0;
189	      const b = Math.abs(Math.sin(p * Math.PI * 2));
190	      this.scaleX = 1 - b * 0.12;
191	      this.scaleY = 1 + b * 0.18;
192	    }
193	  }
194	
195	  die() {
196	    this.move(0);
197	    this.dead = true;
198	    this.facing = 'dead';
199	    this.setTexture('hero-dead');
200	    this.setScale(1, 1);
201	    this.setAngle(0);
202	    this.shadow.setVisible(false);
203	  }
204	}

     1	import * as Phaser from 'phaser';
     2	import { GAME_W, GAME_H, GROUND_Y, GROUND_H, PALETTES, SCALE } from '../config.js';
     3	import { Sfx } from '../audio.js';
     4	
     5	// Tween a value from one packed-hex color to another, calling apply(color) each
     6	// frame. Used for the smooth arena recolor on every palette change.
     7	function tweenColor(scene, fromInt, toInt, apply, duration = 500) {
     8	  const from = Phaser.Display.Color.IntegerToColor(fromInt);
     9	  const to = Phaser.Display.Color.IntegerToColor(toInt);
    10	  scene.tweens.addCounter({
    11	    from: 0,
    12	    to: 100,
    13	    duration,
    14	    onUpdate: (tw) => {
    15	      const c = Phaser.Display.Color.Interpolate.ColorWithColor(from, to, 100, tw.getValue());
    16	      apply(Phaser.Display.Color.GetColor(c.r, c.g, c.b));
    17	    },
    18	  });
    19	}

    21	// Owns all non-gameplay visuals: paper background, notebook grid, water strip,

292	    this.heartObjs.forEach((h, i) => {
293	      if (i < this.lives) h.setVisible(true).setPosition(startX + i * gap, y);
294	      else h.setVisible(false);
295	    });
296	    this.chargerBg.setVisible(charging);
297	    this.chargerFill.setVisible(charging);
298	    if (charging) {
299	      const cx = startX + this.lives * gap;
300	      this.chargerBg.setPosition(cx, y);
301	      this.chargerFill.setPosition(cx, y);
302	    }
303	  }
304	
305	  // frac: 0..1 progress to the next heart — fill the heart shape bottom-up.
306	  updateCharger(frac) {
307	    if (this.mode !== 'lives' || !this.chargerFill.visible) return;
308	    const fw = this.chargerFill.frame.width;
309	    const fh = this.chargerFill.frame.height;
310	    // The heart occupies ~16%..82% of the texture height (see makeHeart).
311	    const top = 0.16 * fh;
312	    const bot = 0.82 * fh;
313	    const f = Phaser.Math.Clamp(frac, 0, 1);
314	    const visTop = bot - f * (bot - top);
315	    this.chargerFill.setCrop(0, visTop, fw, bot - visTop);
316	  }
317	
318	  // Bank a heart (filled charger or heart drop), capped, with a pop + chime.
319	  gainLife() {
320	    if (this.mode !== 'lives' || this.lives >= this.maxLives) return false;
321	    this.lives += 1;
322	    this.layoutHearts();
323	    Sfx.heart();
324	    const h = this.heartObjs[this.lives - 1];
325	    this.tweens.add({
326	      targets: h,
327	      scaleX: { from: this.heartScale * 1.6, to: this.heartScale },
328	      scaleY: { from: this.heartScale * 1.6, to: this.heartScale },
329	      duration: 320,
330	      ease: 'Back.out',
331	    });
332	    return true;
333	  }
334	
335	  // Feed the charging heart; each full 10 banks a life (carrying the remainder).
336	  addHeartProgress(amount) {
337	    if (this.mode !== 'lives') return;
338	    this.heartProgress += amount;
339	    while (this.heartProgress >= 10 && this.lives < this.maxLives) {
340	      this.heartProgress -= 10;
341	      this.gainLife();
342	    }
343	    if (this.lives >= this.maxLives) this.heartProgress = 0;
344	  }
345	
346	  // A ball touched the hero. In lives mode with lives to spare, lose one and
347	  // become briefly invincible (balls keep flying); otherwise it's game over.
348	  onHit() {
349	    if (this.over || this.invincible) return;
350	    if (this.mode === 'lives' && this.lives > 1) {
351	      this.lives -= 1;
352	      this.layoutHearts();
353	      this.hurt();
354	    } else {
355	      this.die();
356	    }
357	  }
358	
359	  // Non-fatal hit: flash + blink + short invincibility, no freeze.
360	  hurt() {
361	    this.invincible = true;
362	    Sfx.hurt();
363	    this.cameras.main.shake(150, 0.006);
364	    const blink = this.tweens.add({ targets: this.player, alpha: 0.3, duration: 110, yoyo: true, repeat: -1 });
365	    this.time.delayedCall(INVINCIBLE_MS, () => {
366	      blink.stop();
367	      this.player.setAlpha(1);
368	      this.invincible = false;
369	    });
370	  }
371	
372	  die() {

379	    // Clear the heart HUD so it reads empty on the game-over screen (the last

381	    if (this.mode === 'lives' && this.heartObjs) {

392	      angle: { min: 0, max: 360 },
393	      lifespan: 800,

17	    },
18	  });
19	}

    11	export function makeDoodleButton(scene, x, y, label, color, onClick) {

    13	    .text(0, 0, label, {

    24	  const h = text.height + padY * 2;
    25	  const bg = scene.add.rectangle(0, 0, w, h, color).setStrokeStyle(3 * SCALE, 0x2b2b2b);
    26	
    27	  const btn = scene.add.container(x, y, [bg, text]);
    28	  bg.setInteractive({ useHandCursor: true });

     4	// are just different draws — no external art assets required.

     7	// SCALE so the hand-drawn look stays consistent at the high-res buffer.
     8	import rough from 'roughjs';

    10

    13	
    14	function makeCanvas(w, h) {

     1	# Backlog
     2	
     3	Ideas captured for later, with enough notes to pick up cold.
     4	
     5	## Rewind mode (time-rollback continue)
     6	
     7	**Idea:** A third game mode where, instead of losing a life outright, death lets you
     8	*rewind* a second or two to just before the fatal hit and resume (with brief
     9	invincibility). Distinct from Lives mode — here the ball trajectories are *rewound*
    10	too, not just continued.
    11	
    12	**Why it's harder than Lives mode:** Lives mode only needs a flag + invincibility
    13	timer; the world keeps running forward. Rewind needs the world to actually go
    14	*backwards*, which means recording and restoring full simulation state.
    15	
    16	**Sketch:**
    17	- Keep a ring buffer of world snapshots, ~1 per frame for the last ~2–3s
    18	  (e.g. 180 frames). Each snapshot stores: player x; every ball's
    19	  `{textureKey, x, y, vx, vy, angularVelocity, scale}`; every pickup's
    20	  `{value, x, y, vx, vy}`; `elapsed`/`collected`/`segment`.
    21	- On death: pick the snapshot from ~1.2s before now, then rebuild the scene from it
    22	  — destroy current balls/pickups, recreate from the snapshot (Arcade physics isn't
    23	  deterministic to *replay*, but restoring a position+velocity snapshot is exact),
    24	  rewind `elapsed`/score, grant invincibility, resume.
    25	- Optional polish: a visual "rewind" effect (fast-reverse a few frames by stepping
    26	  the buffer backwards before resuming, desaturate/scanline shader, a whoosh SFX).
    27	- Limit uses (e.g. N rewinds per run) so it's not infinite, like Lives.
    28	
    29	**Cost / risk:** Memory for the buffer is small (a few hundred plain objects).
    30	Main work is a clean serialize/restore of Ball/NumberPickup (their constructors take
    31	indices, not raw state — would need a `fromSnapshot()` path or a restore method that
    32	bypasses `launch()`/`configure()`). Moderate effort; well-contained.
    33	
    34	**Full plan:** see [docs/rewind-mode-plan.md](docs/rewind-mode-plan.md).
    35	
    36	**Status:** Not started. Lives mode (shipped, now with a heart economy) covers the
    37	"more forgiving" need for now.
=====README=====
     1	# Attack on Ball
     2	
     3	A doodle-style recreation of the classic **Attack on Ball** arcade game (originally
     4	by *eggbones*, last updated 2017 and effectively gone from modern stores). Built
     5	with **Phaser 4**, rendered in a hand-drawn "crayon" look with **rough.js**, and
     6	shipped as an installable **PWA**.
     7	
     8	**▶ Play: https://daviddwlee84.github.io/AttackOnBall/**
     9	
    10	![hero](public/icons/icon-192.png)
    11	
    12	## Gameplay
    13	
    14	Move the green hero left/right along the water line. Balls of various sizes fly in
    15	from both sides and bounce around the arena — get hit and it's game over. Survive
    16	as long as you can: the timer (your score) counts up continuously, and walking over
    17	the falling numbers adds those seconds straight to it. Every 10 seconds the arena
    18	recolors. Difficulty ramps up: balls spawn faster and more pile on the longer you
    19	last. Every ball is guaranteed to bounce above the hero's head, so it's always
    20	dodgeable.
    21	
    22	**Controls**
    23	
    24	- Desktop: `←` / `→` or `A` / `D`
    25	- Touch: tap or hold anywhere — the hero walks toward your finger
    26	
    27	**Settings (start screen)** — pick a difficulty preset (Easy / Medium / Hard / Crazy)
    28	or open **Advanced settings** to tune move speed, gravity, ball speed/angle, spawn
    29	rates and the difficulty ramp. Settings persist in the browser.
    30	
    31	## Develop
    32	
    33	```bash
    34	npm install
    35	npm run dev       # local dev server with hot reload
    36	npm run build     # production build to dist/
    37	npm run preview   # serve the production build locally
    38	npm run smoke      # headless boot/play check against the preview server
    39	```
    40	
    41	> `npm run smoke` requires the preview server running (`npm run preview`) and
    42	> installs Puppeteer on demand; it is optional and CI-style only.
    43	
    44	## Architecture
    45	
    46	- `src/config.js` — fixed constants (render `SCALE`, arena size, palettes, ball
    47	  sizes, pickup values). The whole game is authored at 960×540 and multiplied by
    48	  `SCALE` for a crisp hi-DPI buffer.
    49	- `src/settings.js` — runtime-configurable, persisted settings: difficulty presets
    50	  + advanced physics/difficulty params. `gameParams()` returns SCALE-applied values
    51	  the gameplay reads (via `scene.params`).
    52	- `src/ui/settingsPanel.js` — the HTML settings overlay on the menu screen.
    53	- `src/doodle.js` — rough.js texture generators (hero expressions, balls, numbers,
    54	  fragments, grid). All art is generated procedurally at boot — no image assets.
    55	- `src/scenes/` — `BootScene` (generates textures) → `MenuScene` (backdrop +
    56	  settings panel) → `GameScene` (core loop) → `GameOverScene`.
    57	- `src/objects/` — `Player`, `Ball`, `NumberPickup`.
    58	- `src/systems/` — `spawner` (difficulty/density) and `arena` (background, timer
    59	  bar, palette shuffle).
    60	
    61	The original vanilla-Canvas prototype lives in `deprecated/attack_on_ball_canvas.html`
    62	for reference; the tuned physics constants were ported from it.
    63	
    64	## Deploy to GitHub Pages
    65	
    66	Already live (see link above). `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds with the
    67	`/AttackOnBall/` base path (`GITHUB_PAGES=true`) and deploys `dist/` via GitHub
    68	Actions on every push to `main`. Pages is configured with **Source: GitHub Actions**.
    69	If you fork/rename, update `base` in `vite.config.js` to match the new repo name.
```

1	import * as Phaser from 'phaser';
2	import { SCALE } from '../config.js';
3	
4	// A rounded doodle-style text button. Returns a container (for easy positioning
5	// + alpha tweening); the background rectangle carries the interactivity.
6	//
7	// NOTE: we make the *rectangle child* interactive rather than giving the
8	// container a custom hitArea — a container-level Geom hitArea does not
9	// hit-test reliably in Phaser (the pointer never registers as "over"), which
10	// silently breaks clicks.
11	export function makeDoodleButton(scene, x, y, label, color, onClick) {
12	  const text = scene.add
13	    .text(0, 0, label, {
14	      fontFamily: '"Comic Sans MS", "Marker Felt", sans-serif',
15	      fontSize: `${24 * SCALE}px`,
16	      color: '#08334d',
17	      fontStyle: 'bold',
18	    })
19	    .setOrigin(0.5);
20	
21	  const padX = 30 * SCALE;
22	  const padY = 14 * SCALE;
23	  const w = text.width + padX * 2;
24	  const h = text.height + padY * 2;
25	  const bg = scene.add.rectangle(0, 0, w, h, color).setStrokeStyle(3 * SCALE, 0x2b2b2b);
26	
27	  const btn = scene.add.container(x, y, [bg, text]);
28	  bg.setInteractive({ useHandCursor: true });
29	  bg.on('pointerover', () => btn.setScale(1.04));
30	  bg.on('pointerout', () => btn.setScale(1));
31	  if (onClick) bg.on('pointerdown', onClick);
32	
33	  btn.bg = bg;
34	  return btn;
35	}
36

/**
 * Transparent notebook-grid overlay (drawn once, tinted per palette at runtime).
 */
export function makeGrid(scene, key, w, h, gap = 40 * S) {
  const canvas = makeCanvas(w, h);
  const rc = rough.canvas(canvas);
  const opts = { roughness: 1.2, bowing: 0.8, stroke: '#ffffff', strokeWidth: 1.5 * S };
  for (let x = gap; x < w; x += gap) rc.line(x, 0, x, h, opts);
  for (let y = gap; y < h; y += gap) rc.line(0, y, w, y, opts);
  register(scene, key, canvas);
}

// A lightweight in-game debug HUD: current FPS (smoothed), the worst FPS in the

// last ~N frames. Frame time is measured from wall-clock `performance.now()` so
// real stutters (long frames) show up as sharp dips, instead of being hidden by
// Phaser's smoothed average. Toggle from GameScene (F3 / settings).
const N = 150; // samples kept in the graph (~2.5s at 60fps)
const MAX_FPS = 70; // graph vertical scale

export default class DebugOverlay {
  constructor(scene) {
    this.scene = scene;
    this.visible = false;
    this.buf = [];
    this.lastNow = null;
    this.lastFrameMs = 0;
    this.textAccum = 0;

    this.x = 16 * SCALE;
    this.y = 60 * SCALE;
    this.w = 250 * SCALE;
    this.h = 112 * SCALE;

    this.gw = this.w - 2 * this.pad;

## Overview

Phaser 4 + Vite ESM project, no TypeScript, all art procedurally generated with rough.js at boot. Everything is authored at 960×540 "design units" and multiplied by `SCALE = 2` → a fixed 1920×1080 backing buffer.

**File structure**

```
index.html                    223 L  loading screen, rotate prompt, install banner, CSS
vite.config.js                 37 L  base path + VitePWA manifest
package.json                          phaser ^4, roughjs ^4.6.6, zzfx; vite 6, vite-plugin-pwa, puppeteer-core
src/main.js                    31 L  Phaser.Game config (scale/physics/scene list)
src/config.js                  65 L  fixed constants (SCALE, arena, ball sizes, palettes)
src/settings.js                96 L  difficulty presets + advanced params, localStorage
src/doodle.js                 321 L  rough.js texture generators, exports PAD
src/audio.js                  125 L  ZzFX sfx + music, mute
src/pwa-install.js             89 L  A2HS banner
src/scenes/BootScene.js        44 L  generates all textures → MenuScene
src/scenes/MenuScene.js        48 L  backdrop + HTML settings panel
src/scenes/GameScene.js       411 L  core loop
src/scenes/PauseScene.js       42 L  overlay
src/scenes/GameOverScene.js    93 L  best score + restart
src/objects/Player.js         204 L
src/objects/Ball.js           106 L
src/objects/NumberPickup.js    42 L
src/objects/HeartPickup.js     40 L
src/systems/spawner.js         61 L  difficulty driver
src/systems/arena.js           97 L  bg/grid/water/score bar/palette
src/ui/settingsPanel.js       304 L  HTML overlay (presets + advanced sliders)
src/ui/button.js               35 L  makeDoodleButton

scripts/{smoke-test,generate-icons,generate-og}.mjs
deprecated/attack_on_ball_canvas.html   original vanilla-canvas prototype
docs/rewind-mode-plan.md, BACKLOG.md
.github/workflows/deploy.yml   Node 22, GITHUB_PAGES=true → Pages
```

Build: `npm run dev|build|preview|smoke|icons|og`. Base path `/AttackOnBall/` when `GITHUB_PAGES` is set (`vite.config.js:37`).

---

## 1. Difficulty system

**Presets — `/home/daviddwlee84/Documents/Program/Personal/AttackOnBall/src/settings.js:13-18`**

```js
export const PRESETS = {
  easy:   { playerSpeed: 400, ballSpeedMin: 420, ballSpeedMax: 720,  spawnStart: 2.2,  spawnMin: 0.8,  spawnRamp: 0.012, doubleAfter: 35, tripleAfter: 80, densityRamp: 55 },
  medium: { playerSpeed: 380, ballSpeedMin: 560, ballSpeedMax: 1000, spawnStart: 1.6,  spawnMin: 0.35, spawnRamp: 0.022, doubleAfter: 18, tripleAfter: 45, densityRamp: 35 },
  hard:   { playerSpeed: 380, ballSpeedMin: 700, ballSpeedMax: 1200, spawnStart: 1.2,  spawnMin: 0.28, spawnRamp: 0.03,  doubleAfter: 10, tripleAfter: 28, densityRamp: 25 },
  crazy:  { playerSpeed: 360, ballSpeedMin: 880, ballSpeedMax: 1500, spawnStart: 0.85, spawnMin: 0.2,  spawnRamp: 0.045, doubleAfter: 5,  tripleAfter: 14, densityRamp: 14 },
};
```

**Not controlled by presets** — `settings.js:24-32` `ADVANCED_DEFAULTS`: `gravity: 1000`, `ballBounce: 1`, `angleMin: 40`, `angleMax: 78`, `minApexClearance: 40`, `speedRamp: 0.006`, `speedRampCap: 0.6`.

This is the root of the user's "Easy balls should bounce higher / Crazy balls fly across" complaint: **gravity, bounce and launch angle are identical across all four presets**, so Easy's slower balls produce a *lower* apex (apex = (v·sinθ)²/2g) and Crazy's fast balls have huge horizontal velocity and cross the arena in one or two bounces.

Other pieces:
- `settings.js:34` `DEFAULT_DIFFICULTY = 'medium'`; `settings.js:37-48` `PREF_DEFAULTS` (mode/lives/autoRecover/heartDropChance/audio/debug).
- `settings.js:50-52` `defaults()`, `:54-64` `load()` (key `'aob-settings'`), `:66-78` `getSettings/setSettings`, `:80-82` `applyPreset`, `:84-86` `resetSettings`.
- `settings.js:89-96` `SPATIAL = ['playerSpeed','gravity','ballSpeedMin','ballSpeedMax','minApexClearance']` — multiplied by `SCALE` in `gameParams()`. Note `spawnStart/spawnMin/ramps/angles/ballBounce` are **not** scaled (correct — they're time/ratio/angle).
- `GameScene.create()` snapshots once per run: `src/scenes/GameScene.js:31` `this.params = gameParams()`. Changing settings mid-run has no effect.
- UI: `src/ui/settingsPanel.js:17` (`COMMON`, move speed 200–600), `:20-36` (`ADVANCED` slider specs with min/max/step), `:106` any preset-key edit flips `difficulty` to `'custom'`, `:161-169` preset buttons.

**Scaling / growth over time — all linear, no easing:**

| Curve | Location | Formula |
|---|---|---|
| Spawn interval | `src/systems/spawner.js:20` | `interval = max(spawnMin, spawnStart - elapsed*spawnRamp)` |
| 2nd ball chance | `spawner.js:26` | `elapsed > doubleAfter && rand() < (elapsed-doubleAfter)/densityRamp` |
| 3rd ball chance | `spawner.js:27` | same with `tripleAfter` |
| Ball launch speed | `src/objects/Ball.js:106` | `ramp = 1 + min(speedRampCap, elapsed*speedRamp)` |

Because the density probability is uncapped, once `elapsed > doubleAfter + densityRamp` **every** spawn tick is 2 balls (and 3 after `tripleAfter + densityRamp`) — a hard step, not a taper. Speed ramp saturates at +60 % at t=100 s with defaults.

---

## 2. Ball spawning & physics

**Creation** — `src/systems/spawner.js:39-45`:
```js
spawnBall(elapsed) {
  const sizeIdx = Phaser.Math.Between(0, BALL_SIZES.length - 1);   // uniform over 4 sizes
  const colorIdx = Phaser.Math.Between(0, BALL_COLORS.length - 1);
  const ball = new Ball(this.scene, sizeIdx, colorIdx);
  this.scene.balls.add(ball);

`/home/daviddwlee84/Documents/Program/Personal/AttackOnBall/src/objects/Player.js:11-44` (constructor):

**Input** — `src/scenes/GameScene.js:82-84` (cursors + A/D) and `readDirection()` at **`GameScene.js:112-123`**:
```js

  if (this.cursors.right.isDown || this.keyD.isDown) return 1;

There is **no tilt/deviceorientation handling at all** (grep for `deviceorientation`/`DeviceMotion` returns nothing).

**Bounds analysis for the "invisible wall on the right" bug** — three independent limits stack:

1. `setCollideWorldBounds(true)` + body width `0.7*PLAYER_SIZE`: max `player.x = GAME_W - 0.35*PLAYER_SIZE` = 1920 − 39.2 ≈ **1880.8** (~2 % of width). Small, but real.
2. **Touch is "walk toward the finger", so the hero can never go further right than the finger's mapped `worldX` minus the 12 px dead zone** (`GameScene.js:120`). To touch the far-right column you must physically press the far-right edge of the canvas — which on Android is the back-gesture edge and on iOS the swipe/home-indicator strip, so those touches are frequently swallowed by the OS. This is the most likely mechanism for the reported wall (it would be absent on desktop keyboard, matching "手機最右").
3. **A hard 240 × 180 world-px dead rectangle in the top-right** (`GameScene.js:118`, `x > GAME_W-240 && y < 180`) — 12.5 % of the width × 16.7 % of the height literally returns `0` (no movement) — that IS an invisible wall if the player's thumb rides high on the right side.

Also relevant: no `resize`/`orientation` listener exists (see §5), so a stale input bounds mapping after rotation is a fourth candidate. There is no code that offsets/clamps the player other than the three above.

## 4. Restart / reset

- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.js:82-86` `restart()` → `scene.stop('GameScene'); scene.stop(); scene.start('GameScene')`.
- `src/scenes/PauseScene.js:165-168` "↻ Restart" → `scene.stop(); scene.start('GameScene')` (note: does **not** stop `GameScene` first — it's paused, and `start` on a paused scene restarts it).
- Reset state all lives in `GameScene.create()` (`:31-46`): fresh `params`, `elapsed/collected/score/segment = 0`, `over = false`, new `Arena`, new `Player(this, GAME_W/2)` (`:54`), new groups, new `Spawner`.
- Test hook `window.__aob = this` at `:109`.

**"Character jumps right on restart" — root cause chain:**

`src/ui/button.js:31` — `if (onClick) bg.on('pointerdown', onClick);` — the buttons fire on **pointerdown, not pointerup**. So `scene.start('GameScene')` runs while the finger/mouse is *still held down*. On the very first `GameScene.update()` frames, `readDirection()` (`GameScene.js:112-123`) sees `activePointer.isDown === true` at the button's last position and returns `Math.sign(pointer.worldX - GAME_W/2)`, so the freshly spawned hero immediately walks toward the button. The "▶ Play Again" button (`GameOverScene.js:65`) is centered at `GAME_W/2` but is `text.width + 2*30*SCALE` wide (≈420 px at SCALE 2), so any tap right of its centre gives a rightward `dx` for the remaining touch duration (~100–200 ms × 760 px/s ≈ 75–150 px jump). Same applies to PauseScene's restart button (`PauseScene.js:165`).

Contributing factors: nothing clears/ignores the pointer state across the scene transition, `GameScene` has no `init()` grace period, and there is no "ignore pointer until the next pointerup" guard (the GameOverScene has a 450 ms *arming* delay at `:73` but nothing on the outgoing side).

```md
# Attack on Ball — screen adaptation, difficulty rework, leaderboard, dodgeability guarantee

## Context

After playing the shipped game, two bugs and several design gaps surfaced:

1. **Screen fit.** The game is authored at a fixed 960×540 design surface (`SCALE=2` →
   1920×1080 buffer) and displayed with `Phaser.Scale.FIT` (`src/main.js:22-25`). On a
   19.5:9 phone in landscape that letterboxes into dead strips left and right. Combined
   with a 240×180-world-px "ignore taps" rectangle in the top-right of `readDirection()`
   (`src/scenes/GameScene.js:118`) and the touch-follow control scheme (the hero can never
   go further right than your finger), the far right of the screen behaves like an
   **invisible wall**.
2. **Restart jerks right.** `makeDoodleButton` binds its callback to `pointerdown`
   (`src/ui/button.js:31`). "▶ Play Again" / "↻ Restart" therefore starts `GameScene`
   while the finger is still down; on the first frames `readDirection()` sees
   `activePointer.isDown` at the button position and walks the fresh hero toward it.
3. **Difficulty presets don't deliver their promise.** `gravity`, `ballBounce` and
   `angleMin/Max` are identical for every preset (`src/settings.js:24-32`); only speed
   changes. Since apex = (v·sinθ)²/2g, *Easy's slow balls arc lowest* and get clamped to
   the bare `minApexClearance` minimum — barely above the hero's head, so they're hard to
   dodge. *Crazy's fast balls* get huge vx and cross the whole arena in one arc without
   ever bouncing inside it. Growth curves are all linear-then-clamped, and the extra-ball
   probability is uncapped, so after `doubleAfter + densityRamp` seconds *every* tick
   spawns 2 balls — a step, not a taper.
4. **No per-difficulty ranking**, no landing-point prediction, and no formal answer to
   "is this run actually survivable?".

Intended outcome: the game fills any screen and any window, presents landscape without
the player having to physically rotate, each difficulty preset feels the way its name
promises, runs are provably dodgeable, and scores are ranked top-10 per difficulty.

Deferred ideas (Super Crazy / bullet-hell, joystick + drag control modes, 搞笑模式, power-ups,
double-tap dash) go to `BACKLOG.md` — see the final phase.

---

## Phase 1 — Responsive arena (full-bleed on any screen)

**Goal:** the design surface matches the real viewport aspect, so `Scale.FIT` no longer
letterboxes and every pixel of the screen is playable.

**`src/config.js`**
- Keep `GAME_H = 540 * SCALE` fixed (so hero size, gravity, apex heights and the HUD are
  unchanged everywhere) and make the width dynamic:
  \```js
  export let GAME_W = 960 * SCALE;
  export const ASPECT_MIN = 4 / 3, ASPECT_MAX = 21 / 9;
  export function recomputeArenaSize(w = window.innerWidth, h = window.innerHeight) {
    const a = Phaser.Math.Clamp(w / h, ASPECT_MIN, ASPECT_MAX);
    const next = Math.round(GAME_H * a / 2) * 2;
    const changed = next !== GAME_W;
    GAME_W = next;
    return changed;
  }
  \```
  `export let` gives ES **live bindings**, so every existing `import { GAME_W }` call site
  (Ball, NumberPickup, HeartPickup, GameScene, arena, MenuScene, PauseScene, GameOverScene,
  BootScene) picks up the new value with **zero edits**. Do the clamp math without Phaser
  so `config.js` stays import-light.
- Add `MAX_GAME_W = Math.round(GAME_H * ASPECT_MAX)` for texture sizing.

**`src/main.js`** — call `recomputeArenaSize()` before `new Phaser.Game({...})`.

**`src/scenes/BootScene.js`** — generate the grid once at `MAX_GAME_W` instead of `GAME_W`
(`makeGrid(this, 'grid', MAX_GAME_W, GAME_H)`). The grid image is drawn at origin (0,0)
(`src/systems/arena.js:30-35`), so extra width simply falls off the right edge — no
regeneration on resize, no rough.js cost on rotate.

**Resize handling** — new `src/systems/viewport.js`:
- Listen for `resize` / `orientationchange` (debounced ~150 ms).
- If `recomputeArenaSize()` returns `true`: call `game.scale.resize(GAME_W, GAME_H)` and
  emit an app-level event.
- `MenuScene` restarts itself on that event (cheap, it's just a backdrop).
- `GameScene` **does not** restart mid-run — it re-lays-out instead: `arena.relayout()`
  (bar width, score/HUD x), `layoutHearts()`, pause/mute button x, and
  `this.physics.world.setBounds(0, 0, GAME_W, GAME_H)`. Add `Arena.relayout()` next to the
  existing `setBar`/`setScore` methods. Mid-run resize is an edge case (desktop window
  drag); correctness matters more than perfection.
- `GameScene.create()` must call `this.physics.world.setBounds(...)` explicitly — Phaser
  seeds world bounds from the game config, which is stale after any resize.

**Hero edge reachability** — `src/objects/Player.js:18`. `setCollideWorldBounds(true)` with
a `0.7 * PLAYER_SIZE` body stops the hero's centre `0.35 * PLAYER_SIZE` short of each edge.
Give the player its own expanded bounds so its *centre* can reach the arena edges minus a
small pad:
\```js
const inset = PLAYER_SIZE * 0.35 - EDGE_PAD;   // EDGE_PAD ≈ 6 * SCALE
this.body.setBoundsRectangle(new Phaser.Geom.Rectangle(-inset, 0, GAME_W + 2 * inset, GAME_H));
\```
Safe because balls and pickups don't use world bounds at all (they only collide with the
`this.ground` static body, `GameScene.js:73-74`).

**Notch / safe area** — with full-bleed the canvas now runs under the notch and home
indicator. Read `env(safe-area-inset-left/right)` once via a probe element in
`viewport.js`, convert to design units, and inset the pause/mute buttons (`makePauseButton`,
`makeMuteButton`) and the score text accordingly. Gameplay area stays full width.

## Phase 2 — Input bugs

**`src/ui/button.js`** — fire on release, not press:
\```js
let armed = false;
bg.on('pointerdown', () => { armed = true; });
bg.on('pointerout',  () => { armed = false; btn.setScale(1); });
bg.on('pointerup',   () => { if (armed) { armed = false; onClick?.(); } });
\```
This alone kills the restart jerk for both `GameOverScene.restart()` and `PauseScene`'s
"↻ Restart".

**`src/scenes/GameScene.js` — pointer arming guard** (belt and braces, also covers the HTML
"▶ Play" button in `settingsPanel.js`): in `create()`, `this.pointerArmed = !this.input.activePointer.isDown;`
and at the top of `readDirection()`:
\```js
if (!this.pointerArmed) { if (!this.input.activePointer.isDown) this.pointerArmed = true; return 0; }
\```

**Delete the top-right dead rectangle** (`GameScene.js:118`) — it is a literal invisible
wall over 12.5% × 16.7% of the arena. Replace it with an explicit UI-capture flag: in
`makePauseButton` / `makeMuteButton`, `bg.on('pointerdown', () => { this.uiHold = true; })`,
and clear it with a scene-level `this.input.on('pointerup', () => { this.uiHold = false; })`.
`readDirection()` returns `0` while `this.uiHold` is set.

**Verify** that after these three changes the hero is stationary for the first ~500 ms of a
restart (assert in the smoke test, Phase 7).

## Phase 3 — Default landscape without asking the user to rotate

New `src/orientation.js`, called from the menu's `onPlay` handler
(`src/scenes/MenuScene.js:36-43`) — it must run inside the user gesture:

1. **Preferred path:** `await document.documentElement.requestFullscreen()` then
   `await screen.orientation.lock('landscape')`. Works on Android Chrome and installed
   PWAs (the manifest already declares `orientation: 'landscape'`, `vite.config.js:21`).
   Wrap both in `try/catch` — failure is expected and silent.
2. **Fallback (iOS Safari, where neither API exists):** a `portraitRotate` mode. Add
   `body.aob-rotated` CSS that rotates `#game` by 90° with swapped width/height. Phaser
   derives pointer coordinates from `getBoundingClientRect()`, which returns the *rotated*
   box, so input must be corrected: monkey-patch `game.input.manager.transformPointer` to
   apply the inverse rotation before delegating to the original. This is ~20 lines and
   contained, but it is the **riskiest piece of the plan** — it touches Phaser internals.
   Gate it behind a `portraitRotate` setting (default on, only activated when
   orientation-lock throws) so it can be switched off, and keep the existing
   `#aob-rotate` prompt markup (`index.html:212-215`) as the last-resort fallback: if the
   patch can't be installed, show the prompt as today.
3. Re-run `recomputeArenaSize()` after any orientation change (Phase 1's listener already
   does this).

If the pointer patch proves flaky in testing, ship 1 + the existing rotate prompt and move
the CSS-rotation fallback to the backlog. Report which path landed.

## Phase 4 — Ball flight model, spawn geometry and tapering difficulty

### 4a. Replace speed+angle with apex+crossing-time

The root problem is that `(speed, angle)` couples the two things difficulty actually cares
about. Re-parameterise the launch so each preset controls them independently:

- **`apex`** — height of the ball's *lowest point* at the top of its arc, above the water
  line, in design px. Radius-independent: at the floor the centre sits at `GROUND_Y - r`,
  so the ball's bottom rises exactly `H = vy²/2g`. Therefore `vy = sqrt(2 * g * apex)`.
  Hero head height is `PLAYER_SIZE = 56` design px, so `apex` reads directly as
  "how many hero-heights of clearance".
- **`crossTime`** — seconds to traverse the arena. `vx = (GAME_W + 2 * margin) / crossTime'`
  where `crossTime' = crossTime * (1 + 2*margin/GAME_W)`. Using *time* rather than speed
  keeps difficulty consistent now that `GAME_W` varies per device (Phase 1).
- Bounces inside the arena fall out of the two: `crossTime / (2·sqrt(2·apex/g))`.

New preset keys in `src/settings.js` replacing `ballSpeedMin/ballSpeedMax/angleMin/angleMax`:
`apexMin`, `apexMax`, `crossMin`, `crossMax`. Starting values (design units, g = 1000 —
**playtest and retune**):

| preset | apexMin–apexMax | ≈ hero-heights | crossMin–crossMax (s) | ≈ bounces crossing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| easy   | 150 – 240 | 2.7× – 4.3× | 3.6 – 5.0 | 3.5 – 5   |
| medium | 110 – 190 | 2.0× – 3.4× | 2.4 – 3.4 | 2.5 – 3.5 |
| hard   |  95 – 170 | 1.7× – 3.0× | 1.9 – 2.7 | 2.2 – 3   |
| crazy  |  90 – 150 | 1.6× – 2.7× | 1.5 – 2.2 | 1.7 – 2.5 |

This directly fixes both complaints: **Easy now arcs high** (its slow balls no longer get
squashed onto the `minApexClearance` floor) and **Crazy still bounces inside the arena**
(its pressure comes from ball *count*, not from balls that sail clean over the field).

Keep `minApexClearance` as a hard floor: `apex = max(apex, PLAYER_SIZE + minApexClearance)`,
default `minApexClearance: 20`.

### 4b. Extract launch planning into pure math

Split `Ball.launch()` (`src/objects/Ball.js:43-68`) into:
- `planLaunch(params, sizeIdx, elapsed, rng)` → `{ x, y, vx, vy, r, dir }` — **pure, no
  Phaser, no scene**. Lives in a new `src/systems/ballistics.js`.
- `Ball.applyPlan(plan)` — does the `body.setCircle / setAllowGravity / setGravityY /
  setBounce / setVelocity / setAngularVelocity` work, keeping the existing "must be called
  after group add" contract documented at `Ball.js:38-42`.

`ballistics.js` also exports the helpers Phases 5 and 6 need:
`bouncePeriod(apex, g)`, `heightAt(t, plan, g)`, `xAt(t, plan)`, `timeToFloor(h, vy, g)`.
Keeping it Phaser-free makes it unit-testable from plain Node (Phase 7).

### 4c. Spawn geometry

`src/objects/Ball.js:17-21` currently spawns at `x = ±r` (balls pop in at the very edge)
and `y = GROUND_Y - r - Math.random()*r` (a random height that silently adds energy and
makes the real apex non-deterministic).

- Spawn at `x = -(r + margin)` / `GAME_W + r + margin` with `margin` randomised in a band
  (new `spawnMarginMin`/`spawnMarginMax`, ≈ 40–160 design px). The random margin gives free
  **bounce-phase variety** — balls no longer all enter at the same point of their arc.
- Spawn exactly at `y = GROUND_Y - r` (resting on the floor). Apex is then exactly
  `vy²/2g`, which the landing marker and the safety simulator both depend on.
- `isOffscreen()` (`Ball.js:95-97`) — make the `40` literal `40 * SCALE` and widen the cull
  margin to match the new spawn margin.

### 4d. Tapering growth curves

Replace the linear ramps with asymptotic ones, choosing time constants that **preserve
today's initial slope** so the existing preset numbers port over directly.

| curve | today | new |
|---|---|---|
| spawn interval (`src/systems/spawner.js:20`) | `max(spawnMin, spawnStart - t*spawnRamp)` | `spawnMin + (spawnStart - spawnMin) * exp(-t / spawnTau)`, `spawnTau = (spawnStart - spawnMin)/spawnRamp` |
| 2nd ball (`spawner.js:26`) | `rand() < (t - doubleAfter)/densityRamp` (uncapped → always 2 balls) | `rand() < 0.90 * (1 - exp(-(t - doubleAfter)/densityRamp))` |
| 3rd ball (`spawner.js:27`) | same | `rand() < 0.75 * (1 - exp(-(t - tripleAfter)/densityRamp))` |
| pressure ramp (`Ball.js:45`) | `1 + min(speedRampCap, t*speedRamp)` | `1 + speedRampCap * (1 - exp(-t / speedTau))`, `speedTau = speedRampCap/speedRamp` |

The pressure ramp now shortens `crossTime` (horizontal pressure) and leaves `apex` alone,
so arcs stay readable as the run gets long.

### 4e. Settings panel + migration

- `src/ui/settingsPanel.js`: swap the four `ballSpeed*/angle*` sliders in `ADVANCED`
  (`:23-26`) for `apexMin/apexMax/crossMin/crossMax` + the two spawn-margin sliders.
- Widen the always-visible move-speed slider (`COMMON`, `:17`) from `200–600` to
  `180–900`, per the "更大範圍的調整角色速度" request. (Double-tap dash → backlog.)
- Bump `STORAGE_KEY` to `'aob-settings-v2'` (`settings.js:9`). On first v2 load, carry over
  the preference keys (`mode`, `lives`, `autoRecover`, `heartDropChance`, audio, `debug`)
  from the v1 blob and drop the stale physics keys; anyone on `difficulty: 'custom'` falls
  back to `medium`. Leaving old keys in place via the current `{...defaults(), ...saved}`
  merge would silently keep dead values around.

## Phase 5 — Toggleable landing-point marker

The existing per-ball ellipse (`Ball.js:33-36`) is a *height* shadow directly under the
ball. Add a second, predictive marker showing where it will next touch the ground.

- In `Ball`, alongside `this.shadow`, create `this.marker` — a stroked circle
  (`scene.add.circle(...).setStrokeStyle(...).setFillStyle()`) at depth **−2** (under both
  existing shadows; see the depth table below), stroked in the ball's own colour so you can
  tell which incoming ball it belongs to.
- In `Ball.tick()`, using `ballistics.timeToFloor`: with Phaser's down-positive `vy` and
  `h` = height of the ball's bottom above `GROUND_Y`,
  `t = (vy + sqrt(vy*vy + 2*g*h)) / g`, then `xLand = x + vx * t`. Hide the marker when
  `xLand` falls outside the arena. Fade alpha up as `t → 0` so imminent landings read
  loudest.
- Destroy it in `Ball.destroy()` next to the existing shadow teardown (`Ball.js:99-105`).
- New `landingMarker` setting (default **on**) with a `makeToggle('landingMarker', '🎯 Landing spot')`
  in the settings panel, read once per run through `scene.params` like everything else.
- **Drive-by fix while in `tick()`:** the shadow falloff `260 * (this.radius / 36)`
  (`Ball.js:75`) mixes a design-unit constant with a SCALE-applied radius, so the falloff
  is 2× stronger than intended. Should be `260 * SCALE * (this.radius / (36 * SCALE))`.

Existing depth map for reference: −20 bg, −19 grid, −18 water, −1 ball/player shadows,
0 sprites, 1 dust, 40-43 bar/score, 44-45 hearts, 60-61 popups, 70-72 game over, 80 buttons,
200-201 debug.

## Phase 6 — Per-difficulty top-10 leaderboard

New `src/systems/leaderboard.js`, localStorage key `'aob-scores-v1'`:
\```js
// { "classic:crazy": [{ name, score, ts }, ...] }  — sorted desc, sliced to 10
bucketOf(mode, difficulty)     // 'custom' difficulty gets its own bucket per mode
top(bucket, n = 10)
qualifies(bucket, score)       // board < 10 entries, or score beats the last
submit(bucket, name, score)    // → 1-based rank
\```
Structure the module as a thin sync wrapper over a storage adapter so a hosted backend can
be swapped in later without touching call sites.

- **Name entry:** new `src/ui/nameEntry.js` — an HTML overlay (same approach and CSS idiom

  `playerName` setting so repeat runs are one tap.
- **`GameOverScene`:** after submitting, show `Rank #N` plus the top 3 for the bucket
  alongside the existing Score/Best lines (`GameOverScene.js:44-60`).
- **`settingsPanel.js`:** a `🏆 Top 10` section that renders the board for the currently
  selected mode + difficulty, refreshed from the existing `refresh()` (`:118-132`) so it

  legacy `aob-best-*` values can't be attributed to a difficulty, so don't try to migrate

## Phase 7 — Dodgeability guarantee (`src/systems/safety.js`)

**Yes, this is tractable**, because the problem is one-dimensional: the hero only moves
along x at a constant speed, and every ball's trajectory is closed-form (constant `vx`,
elastic vertical bounce). It reduces to *reachable-interval propagation* — a dilate-then-mask
sweep, not a search.

**Algorithm** (pure math, **no Phaser imports** — takes plain `{x, y, vx, vy, r}` objects):
- Horizon `H = 3.0 s`, step `dt = 1/30` → 90 steps. x discretised into `N = 128` bins across
  the hero's legal range.
- For each step, integrate every live ball forward (`dt` Euler + floor reflection —
  numeric rather than closed-form so it stays correct if `ballBounce < 1`), and mark
  `blocked[i]` where the ball circle intersects the hero AABB (half-width `PLAYER_SIZE*0.35`,
  top `GROUND_Y - PLAYER_SIZE*0.85`) centred on bin `i`, plus a small margin.
- `reach` is a `Uint8Array(N)` seeded at the hero's current bin. Each step:
  dilate by `k = ceil(playerSpeed * dt / binWidth)` bins (O(N) sliding window), then
  `AND NOT blocked`.
- If `reach` is all-zero at any step → the state is a forced death.

**Wiring into `Spawner.spawnBall`:** plan the launch with `planLaunch()` (Phase 4b), test
the candidate against the live ball set, and re-roll up to 6 times; if every candidate
fails, skip that spawn for the tick. Multiple balls in one tick are tested **sequentially**,
each against the state including the previously accepted ones.

**Cost:** worst case ≈ 6 candidates × 90 steps × (≈15 balls + 128-bin dilate) ≈ 80 k
integer ops, a few times per second. Negligible.

**Setting:** `guaranteeDodgeable`, default **on**. With it in place, `minApexClearance` can
be relaxed from a blunt "every ball must clear your head" clamp to a soft floor — low fast
balls become allowed whenever they're provably dodgeable, which is exactly the variety
Crazy mode wants.

**Debug view:** extend `src/ui/debugOverlay.js` with an F4 toggle that draws the reachable
corridor along the ground line and logs the spawn rejection rate, so the system can be
watched while playing.

**Honest limits — state these in the code comment:** it guarantees no *forced* death from
the balls alive at spawn time within a 3 s horizon, assuming optimal play. It does not
account for balls spawned later (each of those is separately checked against the state at
*its* spawn time, so the property composes but isn't a global proof), and it says nothing
about how *hard* a survivable line is to actually execute.

This system is also the prerequisite for the bullet-hell / Super Crazy mode idea.

## Approved Plan:
# Attack on Ball — screen adaptation, difficulty rework, leaderboard, dodgeability guarantee

## Context

After playing the shipped game, two bugs and several design gaps surfaced:

1. **Screen fit.** The game is authored at a fixed 960×540 design surface (`SCALE=2` →
   1920×1080 buffer) and displayed with `Phaser.Scale.FIT` (`src/main.js:22-25`). On a
   19.5:9 phone in landscape that letterboxes into dead strips left and right. Combined
   with a 240×180-world-px "ignore taps" rectangle in the top-right of `readDirection()`
   (`src/scenes/GameScene.js:118`) and the touch-follow control scheme (the hero can never
   go further right than your finger), the far right of the screen behaves like an
   **invisible wall**.
2. **Restart jerks right.** `makeDoodleButton` binds its callback to `pointerdown`
   (`src/ui/button.js:31`). "▶ Play Again" / "↻ Restart" therefore starts `GameScene`
   while the finger is still down; on the first frames `readDirection()` sees
   `activePointer.isDown` at the button position and walks the fresh hero toward it.
3. **Difficulty presets don't deliver their promise.** `gravity`, `ballBounce` and
   `angleMin/Max` are identical for every preset (`src/settings.js:24-32`); only speed
   changes. Since apex = (v·sinθ)²/2g, *Easy's slow balls arc lowest* and get clamped to
   the bare `minApexClearance` minimum — barely above the hero's head, so they're hard to
   dodge. *Crazy's fast balls* get huge vx and cross the whole arena in one arc without
   ever bouncing inside it. Growth curves are all linear-then-clamped, and the extra-ball
   probability is uncapped, so after `doubleAfter + densityRamp` seconds *every* tick
   spawns 2 balls — a step, not a taper.
4. **No per-difficulty ranking**, no landing-point prediction, and no formal answer to
   "is this run actually survivable?".

Intended outcome: the game fills any screen and any window, presents landscape without
the player having to physically rotate, each difficulty preset feels the way its name
promises, runs are provably dodgeable, and scores are ranked top-10 per difficulty.

Deferred ideas (Super Crazy / bullet-hell, joystick + drag control modes, 搞笑模式, power-ups,
double-tap dash) go to `BACKLOG.md` — see the final phase.

---

## Phase 1 — Responsive arena (full-bleed on any screen)

**Goal:** the design surface matches the real viewport aspect, so `Scale.FIT` no longer
letterboxes and every pixel of the screen is playable.

**`src/config.js`**
- Keep `GAME_H = 540 * SCALE` fixed (so hero size, gravity, apex heights and the HUD are
  unchanged everywhere) and make the width dynamic:
  ```js
  export let GAME_W = 960 * SCALE;
  export const ASPECT_MIN = 4 / 3, ASPECT_MAX = 21 / 9;
  export function recomputeArenaSize(w = window.innerWidth, h = window.innerHeight) {
    const a = Phaser.Math.Clamp(w / h, ASPECT_MIN, ASPECT_MAX);
    const next = Math.round(GAME_H * a / 2) * 2;
    const changed = next !== GAME_W;
    GAME_W = next;
    return changed;
  }
  ```
  `export let` gives ES **live bindings**, so every existing `import { GAME_W }` call site
  (Ball, NumberPickup, HeartPickup, GameScene, arena, MenuScene, PauseScene, GameOverScene,
  BootScene) picks up the new value with **zero edits**. Do the clamp math without Phaser
  so `config.js` stays import-light.
- Add `MAX_GAME_W = Math.round(GAME_H * ASPECT_MAX)` for texture sizing.

**`src/main.js`** — call `recomputeArenaSize()` before `new Phaser.Game({...})`.

**`src/scenes/BootScene.js`** — generate the grid once at `MAX_GAME_W` instead of `GAME_W`
(`makeGrid(this, 'grid', MAX_GAME_W, GAME_H)`). The grid image is drawn at origin (0,0)
(`src/systems/arena.js:30-35`), so extra width simply falls off the right edge — no
regeneration on resize, no rough.js cost on rotate.

**Resize handling** — new `src/systems/viewport.js`:
- Listen for `resize` / `orientationchange` (debounced ~150 ms).
- If `recomputeArenaSize()` returns `true`: call `game.scale.resize(GAME_W, GAME_H)` and
  emit an app-level event.
- `MenuScene` restarts itself on that event (cheap, it's just a backdrop).
- `GameScene` **does not** restart mid-run — it re-lays-out instead: `arena.relayout()`
  (bar width, score/HUD x), `layoutHearts()`, pause/mute button x, and
  `this.physics.world.setBounds(0, 0, GAME_W, GAME_H)`. Add `Arena.relayout()` next to the
  existing `setBar`/`setScore` methods. Mid-run resize is an edge case (desktop window
  drag); correctness matters more than perfection.
- `GameScene.create()` must call `this.physics.world.setBounds(...)` explicitly — Phaser
  seeds world bounds from the game config, which is stale after any resize.

**Hero edge reachability** — `src/objects/Player.js:18`. `setCollideWorldBounds(true)` with
a `0.7 * PLAYER_SIZE` body stops the hero's centre `0.35 * PLAYER_SIZE` short of each edge.
Give the player its own expanded bounds so its *centre* can reach the arena edges minus a
small pad:
```js
const inset = PLAYER_SIZE * 0.35 - EDGE_PAD;   // EDGE_PAD ≈ 6 * SCALE
this.body.setBoundsRectangle(new Phaser.Geom.Rectangle(-inset, 0, GAME_W + 2 * inset, GAME_H));
```
Safe because balls and pickups don't use world bounds at all (they only collide with the
`this.ground` static body, `GameScene.js:73-74`).

**Notch / safe area** — with full-bleed the canvas now runs under the notch and home
indicator. Read `env(safe-area-inset-left/right)` once via a probe element in
`viewport.js`, convert to design units, and inset the pause/mute buttons (`makePauseButton`,
`makeMuteButton`) and the score text accordingly. Gameplay area stays full width.

## Phase 2 — Input bugs

**`src/ui/button.js`** — fire on release, not press:
```js
let armed = false;
bg.on('pointerdown', () => { armed = true; });
bg.on('pointerout',  () => { armed = false; btn.setScale(1); });
bg.on('pointerup',   () => { if (armed) { armed = false; onClick?.(); } });
```
This alone kills the restart jerk for both `GameOverScene.restart()` and `PauseScene`'s
"↻ Restart".

**`src/scenes/GameScene.js` — pointer arming guard** (belt and braces, also covers the HTML
"▶ Play" button in `settingsPanel.js`): in `create()`, `this.pointerArmed = !this.input.activePointer.isDown;`
and at the top of `readDirection()`:
```js
if (!this.pointerArmed) { if (!this.input.activePointer.isDown) this.pointerArmed = true; return 0; }
```

**Delete the top-right dead rectangle** (`GameScene.js:118`) — it is a literal invisible
wall over 12.5% × 16.7% of the arena. Replace it with an explicit UI-capture flag: in
`makePauseButton` / `makeMuteButton`, `bg.on('pointerdown', () => { this.uiHold = true; })`,
and clear it with a scene-level `this.input.on('pointerup', () => { this.uiHold = false; })`.
`readDirection()` returns `0` while `this.uiHold` is set.

**Verify** that after these three changes the hero is stationary for the first ~500 ms of a
restart (assert in the smoke test, Phase 7).

## Phase 3 — Default landscape without asking the user to rotate

New `src/orientation.js`, called from the menu's `onPlay` handler
(`src/scenes/MenuScene.js:36-43`) — it must run inside the user gesture:

1. **Preferred path:** `await document.documentElement.requestFullscreen()` then
   `await screen.orientation.lock('landscape')`. Works on Android Chrome and installed
   PWAs (the manifest already declares `orientation: 'landscape'`, `vite.config.js:21`).
   Wrap both in `try/catch` — failure is expected and silent.
2. **Fallback (iOS Safari, where neither API exists):** a `portraitRotate` mode. Add
   `body.aob-rotated` CSS that rotates `#game` by 90° with swapped width/height. Phaser
   derives pointer coordinates from `getBoundingClientRect()`, which returns the *rotated*
   box, so input must be corrected: monkey-patch `game.input.manager.transformPointer` to
   apply the inverse rotation before delegating to the original. This is ~20 lines and
   contained, but it is the **riskiest piece of the plan** — it touches Phaser internals.
   Gate it behind a `portraitRotate` setting (default on, only activated when
   orientation-lock throws) so it can be switched off, and keep the existing
   `#aob-rotate` prompt markup (`index.html:212-215`) as the last-resort fallback: if the
   patch can't be installed, show the prompt as today.
3. Re-run `recomputeArenaSize()` after any orientation change (Phase 1's listener already

## Phase 4 — Ball flight model, spawn geometry and tapering difficulty

### 4a. Replace speed+angle with apex+crossing-time

The root problem is that `(speed, angle)` couples the two things difficulty actually cares
about. Re-parameterise the launch so each preset controls them independently:

- **`apex`** — height of the ball's *lowest point* at the top of its arc, above the water
  line, in design px. Radius-independent: at the floor the centre sits at `GROUND_Y - r`,
  so the ball's bottom rises exactly `H = vy²/2g`. Therefore `vy = sqrt(2 * g * apex)`.
  Hero head height is `PLAYER_SIZE = 56` design px, so `apex` reads directly as
  "how many hero-heights of clearance".
- **`crossTime`** — seconds to traverse the arena. `vx = (GAME_W + 2 * margin) / crossTime'`
  where `crossTime' = crossTime * (1 + 2*margin/GAME_W)`. Using *time* rather than speed
  keeps difficulty consistent now that `GAME_W` varies per device (Phase 1).
- Bounces inside the arena fall out of the two: `crossTime / (2·sqrt(2·apex/g))`.

New preset keys in `src/settings.js` replacing `ballSpeedMin/ballSpeedMax/angleMin/angleMax`:
`apexMin`, `apexMax`, `crossMin`, `crossMax`. Starting values (design units, g = 1000 —
**playtest and retune**):

| preset | apexMin–apexMax | ≈ hero-heights | crossMin–crossMax (s) | ≈ bounces crossing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| easy   | 150 – 240 | 2.7× – 4.3× | 3.6 – 5.0 | 3.5 – 5   |
| medium | 110 – 190 | 2.0× – 3.4× | 2.4 – 3.4 | 2.5 – 3.5 |
| hard   |  95 – 170 | 1.7× – 3.0× | 1.9 – 2.7 | 2.2 – 3   |
| crazy  |  90 – 150 | 1.6× – 2.7× | 1.5 – 2.2 | 1.7 – 2.5 |

This directly fixes both complaints: **Easy now arcs high** (its slow balls no longer get
squashed onto the `minApexClearance` floor) and **Crazy still bounces inside the arena**
(its pressure comes from ball *count*, not from balls that sail clean over the field).

Keep `minApexClearance` as a hard floor: `apex = max(apex, PLAYER_SIZE + minApexClearance)`,
default `minApexClearance: 20`.

### 4b. Extract launch planning into pure math

Split `Ball.launch()` (`src/objects/Ball.js:43-68`) into:
- `planLaunch(params, sizeIdx, elapsed, rng)` → `{ x, y, vx, vy, r, dir }` — **pure, no
  Phaser, no scene**. Lives in a new `src/systems/ballistics.js`.
- `Ball.applyPlan(plan)` — does the `body.setCircle / setAllowGravity / setGravityY /
  setBounce / setVelocity / setAngularVelocity` work, keeping the existing "must be called
  after group add" contract documented at `Ball.js:38-42`.

`ballistics.js` also exports the helpers Phases 5 and 6 need:
`bouncePeriod(apex, g)`, `heightAt(t, plan, g)`, `xAt(t, plan)`, `timeToFloor(h, vy, g)`.
Keeping it Phaser-free makes it unit-testable from plain Node (Phase 7).

### 4c. Spawn geometry

`src/objects/Ball.js:17-21` currently spawns at `x = ±r` (balls pop in at the very edge)
and `y = GROUND_Y - r - Math.random()*r` (a random height that silently adds energy and
makes the real apex non-deterministic).

- Spawn at `x = -(r + margin)` / `GAME_W + r + margin` with `margin` randomised in a band
  (new `spawnMarginMin`/`spawnMarginMax`, ≈ 40–160 design px). The random margin gives free
  **bounce-phase variety** — balls no longer all enter at the same point of their arc.
- Spawn exactly at `y = GROUND_Y - r` (resting on the floor). Apex is then exactly
  `vy²/2g`, which the landing marker and the safety simulator both depend on.
- `isOffscreen()` (`Ball.js:95-97`) — make the `40` literal `40 * SCALE` and widen the cull
  margin to match the new spawn margin.

### 4d. Tapering growth curves

Replace the linear ramps with asymptotic ones, choosing time constants that **preserve
today's initial slope** so the existing preset numbers port over directly.

| curve | today | new |
|---|---|---|
| spawn interval (`src/systems/spawner.js:20`) | `max(spawnMin, spawnStart - t*spawnRamp)` | `spawnMin + (spawnStart - spawnMin) * exp(-t / spawnTau)`, `spawnTau = (spawnStart - spawnMin)/spawnRamp` |
| 2nd ball (`spawner.js:26`) | `rand() < (t - doubleAfter)/densityRamp` (uncapped → always 2 balls) | `rand() < 0.90 * (1 - exp(-(t - doubleAfter)/densityRamp))` |
| 3rd ball (`spawner.js:27`) | same | `rand() < 0.75 * (1 - exp(-(t - tripleAfter)/densityRamp))` |
| pressure ramp (`Ball.js:45`) | `1 + min(speedRampCap, t*speedRamp)` | `1 + speedRampCap * (1 - exp(-t / speedTau))`, `speedTau = speedRampCap/speedRamp` |

The pressure ramp now shortens `crossTime` (horizontal pressure) and leaves `apex` alone,
so arcs stay readable as the run gets long.

### 4e. Settings panel + migration

- `src/ui/settingsPanel.js`: swap the four `ballSpeed*/angle*` sliders in `ADVANCED`
  (`:23-26`) for `apexMin/apexMax/crossMin/crossMax` + the two spawn-margin sliders.
- Widen the always-visible move-speed slider (`COMMON`, `:17`) from `200–600` to
  `180–900`, per the "更大範圍的調整角色速度" request. (Double-tap dash → backlog.)
- Bump `STORAGE_KEY` to `'aob-settings-v2'` (`settings.js:9`). On first v2 load, carry over
  the preference keys (`mode`, `lives`, `autoRecover`, `heartDropChance`, audio, `debug`)
  from the v1 blob and drop the stale physics keys; anyone on `difficulty: 'custom'` falls
  back to `medium`. Leaving old keys in place via the current `{...defaults(), ...saved}`
  merge would silently keep dead values around.

## Phase 5 — Toggleable landing-point marker

The existing per-ball ellipse (`Ball.js:33-36`) is a *height* shadow directly under the
ball. Add a second, predictive marker showing where it will next touch the ground.

- In `Ball`, alongside `this.shadow`, create `this.marker` — a stroked circle
  (`scene.add.circle(...).setStrokeStyle(...).setFillStyle()`) at depth **−2** (under both
  existing shadows; see the depth table below), stroked in the ball's own colour so you can
  tell which incoming ball it belongs to.
- In `Ball.tick()`, using `ballistics.timeToFloor`: with Phaser's down-positive `vy` and
  `h` = height of the ball's bottom above `GROUND_Y`,
  `t = (vy + sqrt(vy*vy + 2*g*h)) / g`, then `xLand = x + vx * t`. Hide the marker when
  `xLand` falls outside the arena. Fade alpha up as `t → 0` so imminent landings read
  loudest.
- Destroy it in `Ball.destroy()` next to the existing shadow teardown (`Ball.js:99-105`).
- New `landingMarker` setting (default **on**) with a `makeToggle('landingMarker', '🎯 Landing spot')`
  in the settings panel, read once per run through `scene.params` like everything else.
- **Drive-by fix while in `tick()`:** the shadow falloff `260 * (this.radius / 36)`
  (`Ball.js:75`) mixes a design-unit constant with a SCALE-applied radius, so the falloff
  is 2× stronger than intended. Should be `260 * SCALE * (this.radius / (36 * SCALE))`.

Existing depth map for reference: −20 bg, −19 grid, −18 water, −1 ball/player shadows,
0 sprites, 1 dust, 40-43 bar/score, 44-45 hearts, 60-61 popups, 70-72 game over, 80 buttons,
200-201 debug.

## Phase 7 — Dodgeability guarantee (`src/systems/safety.js`)

**Yes, this is tractable**, because the problem is one-dimensional: the hero only moves
along x at a constant speed, and every ball's trajectory is closed-form (constant `vx`,
elastic vertical bounce). It reduces to *reachable-interval propagation* — a dilate-then-mask
sweep, not a search.

**Algorithm** (pure math, **no Phaser imports** — takes plain `{x, y, vx, vy, r}` objects):
- Horizon `H = 3.0 s`, step `dt = 1/30` → 90 steps. x discretised into `N = 128` bins across
  the hero's legal range.
- For each step, integrate every live ball forward (`dt` Euler + floor reflection —
  numeric rather than closed-form so it stays correct if `ballBounce < 1`), and mark
  `blocked[i]` where the ball circle intersects the hero AABB (half-width `PLAYER_SIZE*0.35`,
  top `GROUND_Y - PLAYER_SIZE*0.85`) centred on bin `i`, plus a small margin.
- `reach` is a `Uint8Array(N)` seeded at the hero's current bin. Each step:
  dilate by `k = ceil(playerSpeed * dt / binWidth)` bins (O(N) sliding window), then
  `AND NOT blocked`.
- If `reach` is all-zero at any step → the state is a forced death.

**Wiring into `Spawner.spawnBall`:** plan the launch with `planLaunch()` (Phase 4b), test
the candidate against the live ball set, and re-roll up to 6 times; if every candidate
fails, skip that spawn for the tick. Multiple balls in one tick are tested **sequentially**,
each against the state including the previously accepted ones.

**Cost:** worst case ≈ 6 candidates × 90 steps × (≈15 balls + 128-bin dilate) ≈ 80 k
integer ops, a few times per second. Negligible.

**Setting:** `guaranteeDodgeable`, default **on**. With it in place, `minApexClearance` can
be relaxed from a blunt "every ball must clear your head" clamp to a soft floor — low fast
balls become allowed whenever they're provably dodgeable, which is exactly the variety
Crazy mode wants.

**Debug view:** extend `src/ui/debugOverlay.js` with an F4 toggle that draws the reachable
corridor along the ground line and logs the spawn rejection rate, so the system can be
watched while playing.

**Honest limits — state these in the code comment:** it guarantees no *forced* death from
the balls alive at spawn time within a 3 s horizon, assuming optimal play. It does not
account for balls spawned later (each of those is separately checked against the state at
*its* spawn time, so the property composes but isn't a global proof), and it says nothing
about how *hard* a survivable line is to actually execute.

This system is also the prerequisite for the bullet-hell / Super Crazy mode idea.

```javascript
// Keeps the design surface matching the real viewport.
//
// The game is authored at a fixed height (GAME_H) and a *variable* width derived
// from the window's aspect ratio. Phaser then FITs that surface to the screen —
// and because the aspect already matches, there is nothing left to letterbox.
// Without this the 960x540 surface pillarboxes on a 19.5:9 phone in landscape,
// leaving dead strips at both edges that read as invisible walls.
import { GAME_H, GAME_W, recomputeArenaSize } from '../config.js';

// Scene-agnostic event bus for "the arena width changed". Scenes subscribe in
// create() and unsubscribe on shutdown.
const listeners = new Set();

export function onArenaResize(fn) {
  listeners.add(fn);
  return () => listeners.delete(fn);
}

// Safe-area insets (notch / home indicator), in *design units*. With a
// full-bleed canvas the arena now runs underneath them, so HUD corners need to
// stay clear even though gameplay still uses the full width.
let insets = { left: 0, right: 0 };

export function safeInsets() {
  return insets;
}

function measureInsets(displayScale) {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return;
  const probe = document.createElement('div');
  probe.style.cssText =
    'position:fixed;top:0;left:0;width:0;height:0;visibility:hidden;' +
    'padding-left:env(safe-area-inset-left);padding-right:env(safe-area-inset-right);';
  document.body.appendChild(probe);
  const cs = getComputedStyle(probe);
  const leftPx = parseFloat(cs.paddingLeft) || 0;
  const rightPx = parseFloat(cs.paddingRight) || 0;
  probe.remove();
  // CSS px -> design units. displayScale is "design units per CSS px".
  insets = { left: leftPx * displayScale, right: rightPx * displayScale };
}

// Wire the game up to window resize / orientation changes. Debounced, because
// mobile browsers fire a burst of resizes while the URL bar animates.
export function initViewport(game) {
  let timer = null;

  const apply = () => {
    timer = null;
    const changed = recomputeArenaSize();
    // displayScale.x is design-units-per-CSS-px once the canvas has been laid out.
    measureInsets(game.scale.displayScale.x || 1);
    if (!changed) {
      for (const fn of listeners) fn(); // insets may still have moved
      return;
    }
    game.scale.resize(GAME_W, GAME_H);
    for (const fn of listeners) fn();
  };

  const schedule = () => {
    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
    timer = setTimeout(apply, 150);
  };

  window.addEventListener('resize', schedule);
  window.addEventListener('orientationchange', schedule);
  if (screen.orientation) screen.orientation.addEventListener?.('change', schedule);
  // First measurement once the canvas exists.
  game.events.once('ready', apply);
}

```

// Procedural "doodle/crayon" texture generation with rough.js.
// Each helper draws into an offscreen <canvas> and registers it as a Phaser
// texture so sprites can use it like any loaded image. Expressions and colors
// are just different draws — no external art assets required.
//
// Stroke widths, padding and the small fixed-size textures all scale with
// SCALE so the hand-drawn look stays consistent at the high-res buffer.
import rough from 'roughjs';
import { SCALE } from './config.js';

const S = SCALE;
export const PAD = 8 * S; // breathing room so sketchy strokes don't clip the edge

function makeCanvas(w, h) {
  const c = document.createElement('canvas');
  c.width = w;
  c.height = h;
  return c;
}

// Register (or replace) a canvas as a Phaser texture.
function register(scene, key, canvas) {
  if (scene.textures.exists(key)) scene.textures.remove(key);
  scene.textures.addCanvas(key, canvas);
}

// Rounded-rectangle path string, drawn with rough.js for the hand-drawn body.
function roundedRectPath(x, y, w, h, r) {
  return (
    `M${x + r},${y} h${w - 2 * r} a${r},${r} 0 0 1 ${r},${r} ` +
    `v${h - 2 * r} a${r},${r} 0 0 1 ${-r},${r} h${-(w - 2 * r)} ` +
    `a${r},${r} 0 0 1 ${-r},${-r} v${-(h - 2 * r)} a${r},${r} 0 0 1 ${r},${-r} z`
  );
}
